pr.title: Enable GVN for `AggregateKind::RawPtr`
pr.description:
Looks like I was worried for nothing; this seems like it's much easier than I was originally thinking it would be.
r? @cjgillot 

This should be useful for `x[..4]`-like things, should those start inlining enough to expose the lengths.
pr.author: scottmcm

processing.reason: PR #125041 is an optimization-only change: before it, GVN bailed out on `AggregateKind::RawPtr` (`AggregateKind::RawPtr(..) => return None`) and left `PtrMetadata` over such aggregates unfolded. The "incorrect transformation" in the frozen analysis is therefore simply the absence of an optimization, and the new behavior (value-numbering raw-pointer aggregates, folding `PtrMetadata` to `fields[1]`, and skipping only safe thin `PtrToPtr` data-pointer casts) is guarded by the conditions the PR itself documents (`from_mtbl == output_mtbl`, `from_pointee_ty.is_sized`, `to_pointee.is_sized`, ZST metadata → `MemPlaceMeta::None`). No concrete input produces a different observable value between original and transformed semantics; the decoded MIR diffs only show constants/`nop`s replacing redundant moves and a constant `PtrMetadata`, which preserves all values. There is no source-grounded historical miscompile to encode, so any original/transformed pair with different numeric/boolean results would be an artificial, unjustified rewrite rather than a reconstruction of this PR's semantics. Hence no valid counterexample can be provided.

analysis.originalLogic: Before this PR, GVN explicitly treated raw-pointer aggregates as opaque: in `simplify_aggregate` it had `// FIXME: Do the extra work to GVN `from_raw_parts`` followed by `AggregateKind::RawPtr(..) => return None,`. Consequently GVN did not value-number or constant-propagate the two operands of `AggregateKind::RawPtr`, and `UnOp::PtrMetadata` over such an aggregate was not reduced. By contrast, ordinary aggregates (arrays, tuples, closures, ADTs) were already simplified field-by-field.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: Historically GVN performed no rewrite for `AggregateKind::RawPtr`: it bailed out with `return None` and left the raw-pointer aggregate and any `PtrMetadata` on it untouched, even when the data pointer and metadata were already known constants or locals. This was an optimization omission, not a confirmed miscompile: the old output retained `_0 = PtrMetadata(move _4);` and `_0 = *const [i32] from (move _5, move _6);` where the new output produces `_0 = const 1_usize;` and `_0 = *const [i32] from (_2, const 123_usize);`. The new logic value-numbers the aggregate and folds `PtrMetadata` to the metadata field, but only under explicit conditions.
analysis.inputDomain: MIR functions that construct raw pointers via `std::intrinsics::aggregate_raw_ptr` / `from_raw_parts` with a data pointer and a length/metadata operand, especially slice pointers (`*const [T]`) with constant lengths; functions that cast such fat pointers back to thin pointers or to differently-typed thin pointers; functions that call `std::intrinsics::ptr_metadata` on an aggregate raw pointer. Relevant operand types include thin raw pointers, fat raw pointers, metadata of type `usize` (or ZST metadata for sized pointees), and `PtrToPtr` / `PointerCoercion(MutToConstPointer)` casts.
analysis.summary: Optimization PR extending GVN to value-number `AggregateKind::RawPtr` (i.e. `from_raw_parts`/`aggregate_raw_ptr`) and to fold `UnOp::PtrMetadata` over such an aggregate, plus propagation through pointer casts that only change the data pointer. It is an optimization, not a confirmed bug fix. Tests are MIR-dump regression tests under `tests/mir-opt/gvn.rs`.
analysis.trigger: GVN encounters an `Rvalue::Aggregate(AggregateKind::RawPtr(..), field_ops)` with two field operands, or an `UnOp::PtrMetadata` applied to a value already represented as `Value::Aggregate(AggregateTy::RawPtr { .. }, _, fields)`, or a `PtrToPtr` cast whose input is such a raw-pointer aggregate and whose target pointee is sized. The aggregate is also inspected for preceding `PtrToPtr` casts on its data-pointer operand so thin casts can be skipped.
preconditions: The aggregate is `AggregateKind::RawPtr(pointee_ty, mtbl)` and has exactly two field operands; the output pointer type is built as `Ty::new_ptr(self.tcx, pointee_ty, mtbl)`.

Raw-pointer aggregates must be handled specially instead of using `project_field`: the code notes `// Pointers don't have fields, so don't `project_field` them.` and reads field 0 as the data pointer plus field 1 as metadata.

A ZST metadata operand yields `MemPlaceMeta::None` (`if fields[1].layout.is_zst() { MemPlaceMeta::None } else { MemPlaceMeta::Meta(...) }`), so sized-pointee pointers with no metadata are represented correctly.

Cast propagation on the data pointer skips only `PtrToPtr` casts where `from_mtbl == output_mtbl` and `from_pointee_ty.is_sized(self.tcx, self.param_env)`; this matches the comment `// Any thin pointer of matching mutability is fine as the data pointer.`
Folding `PtrMetadata` returns `fields[1]`, the metadata operand, via `(UnOp::PtrMetadata, Value::Aggregate(AggregateTy::RawPtr { .. }, _, fields)) => { return Some(fields[1]); }`.

Casting a raw-pointer aggregate to a sized pointee may drop the metadata only when `to_pointee.is_sized(...)`; the code then uses the aggregate's `data_pointer_ty` and field 0, and if `*data_pointer_ty == to` it returns field 0 directly.
pitfalls: Do not treat a pointer aggregate like a struct and call `project_field`; pointers have no fields, so the special path must read the data pointer and metadata separately.
Do not strip a `PtrToPtr` cast when mutability differs: the condition requires `from_mtbl == output_mtbl`.
Do not strip a cast whose source pointee is unsized: the condition requires `from_pointee_ty.is_sized(...)`, because only thin data pointers may be skipped.
Do not fold `PtrMetadata` to the data pointer field; the metadata is `fields[1]`, not `fields[0]`.
Do not forget ZST metadata handling (`MemPlaceMeta::None`), otherwise sized pointers may be given bogus metadata.

The change is not a general proof that raw-pointer aggregate folding is always safe; the casts-before-aggregate case is guarded by mutability and sizedness, and the fixed tests show constant propagation only when those conditions hold.
analysis.testStrategy: Add focused MIR-dump regression tests in `tests/mir-opt/gvn.rs` using `// EMIT_MIR gvn.<fn>.GVN.diff` with `CHECK-LABEL` / `CHECK` assertions on the post-GVN MIR. Cover four cases: (1) `slice_const_length(&[i32]) -> *const [i32]` with `let len = 123;` checking `_0 = *const [i32] from ({{_[0-9]+}}, const 123_usize);`; (2) `meta_of_ref_to_slice(*const i32) -> usize` using `aggregate_raw_ptr(x, 1)` then `ptr_metadata`, checking `_0 = const 1_usize`; (3) `slice_from_raw_parts_as_ptr(*const u16, usize) -> (*const u16, *const f32)` checking the data-pointer cast `_8 = _1 as *const f32 (PtrToPtr);` and tuple result `_0 = (_1, move _8);`; (4) `casts_before_aggregate_raw_ptr(*const u32) -> *const [u8]` with successive thin casts before `aggregate_raw_ptr(x, 4)`, checking `_0 = *const [u8] from (_1, const 4_usize);`. Also update pre-codegen expectations such as `ptr_offset.demo_byte_add_fat` where the old `_5 = _4 as *const () (PtrToPtr); _6 = PtrMetadata(_1); _0 = *const [u32] from (_5, _6);` becomes `_5 = PtrMetadata(_1); _0 = *const [u32] from (_4, _5);`. Run under both panic-abort and panic-unwind MIR test configurations. No compilation or execution was performed for this knowledge extraction.
evidence: This should be useful for `x[..4]`-like things, should those start inlining enough to expose the lengths.
